title: Isolation of spermatogenic cells from the cynomolgus macaque testis with flow cytometry
protocol: Remove the outer layers, e.g., skin and loose connective tissue.
Detach the epididymis.
Weigh the testis.
Remove the tunica albuginea.
Make a small incision of the tunica albuginea.
Dissect under it to create a dissection plane, separating the seminiferous tubules underneath from the tunica.
Cut the testis tubules into 1 - 2 g pieces.
Submerge testis tubule pieces in 25 mL of Tissue Digest Buffer A.
Leave the samples to digest at 37°C in a water bath for 5 min.
Shake the tube vigorously every 2 min until loosened tubules become visible.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Add 25 mL of Tissue Digest Buffer B and allow the digest to occur for 30 min at 37°C in a water bath.
Shake the tube vigorously every 2 min until dissociation of the tubules into a single-cell suspension of cells.
Add 2.5 mL of FBS to stop digestion.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 25 mL of PBS.
Repeat steps until a single-cell suspension is achieved.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in a desired volume of PBS.
Filter the cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer into a fresh tube.
Count the cells to determine cell concentration.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the matching cell pellet tube with 1 mL of prepared SSEA-4 APC-conjugated Ab stain solution.
Incubate tubes at 37°C for 30 min in the dark.
Agitate tubes every 10 min to resuspend cells.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet.
Wash cells twice with DPBS to remove unbound SSEA-4-APC-conjugated antibodies.
Resuspend cells in DPBS + 10% FBS at a density of 2 to 3 million cells/mL for sorting.
Add 1 μg/mL of PI to the stained cell suspension.
Filter the stained cell suspension using a 40 μm cell strainer.
Keep tubes on ice and protected from light before cell sorting.
Create an FSC-A versus SSC-A contour plot (linear scale).
Draw a "Scatter" gate to include cells of interest while excluding debris.
On the FSC-A versus FSC-H contour plot (linear scale), create a sub-gate under the "Scatter" gate to encompass single cells.
Gate on PI negative live cells using a PI-A (log scale) versus FSC-A (linear scale) contour.
Display all live viable events on a DNA histogram with Hoechst blue on the x-axis and count on the y-axis.
Exclude low Hoechst blue intensity events to omit debris and unstained cells.
Draw a "DNA" gate to include cells containing DNA content of 1C and greater.
View gated “DNA” events on the Hoechst red-A/Hoechst blue-A contour plot (linear scale).
Identify and gate cells in varying stages of spermatogenesis based on DNA content and Hoechst red/Hoechst blue fluorescence profile.
Draw a scatter gate from unstained control to include cells of interest while excluding debris.
Determine baseline voltages for the sample and level of autofluorescence without fluorochromes.
Draw a singlet gate to omit doublets which may contribute to false positives.
Gate on PI negative live cells drawn from PI only control to determine cell viability.
Draw a DNA gate to determine spread of cells based on nucleic acid content from Hoechst only control, and exclude cells less than 1C.
Gates are drawn for the collection of enriched primary spermatocytes based on their stages of meiotic prophase I.
Create 4 gates and label them A, B, C, and D.
These gates represent cell populations enriched in primary spermatocytes at pre-leptotene, leptotene/zygotene, early pachytene, and late pachytene meiotic stages respectively.
Use PI as a nucleic acid stain to enter dead cells with disrupted cell membranes and be excluded from live ones with intact membranes.
Utilize Hoechst 33342 as a live cell dye that enters cells through diffusion and binds to the minor groove of DNA for detection variation in DNA content and chromatin.
Use Hoechst red/blue fluorescence to discriminate subpopulations of cells undergoing meiosis I.
Reliably discriminate live cells (intact PI negative cells) versus non-viable (PI positive) cells using PI.
Discriminate on the DNA content of meiotic cells using Hoechst fluorescence.
Acquire samples using the gating template created for testis cells.
Optimize photomultiplier tube (PMT) voltages using single stain controls in the sequence of unstained, PI only, and Hoechst 33342 only.
Set baseline voltages for the sample with the unstained control to determine autofluorescence level.
Select and gate for singlets from the samples to omit doublets contributing to false positive signals.
Assess cell viability using the PI only control tube by determining percentages of PI negative live cells.
Determine the spread of cells based on their nucleic acid content using the Hoechst 33342 only control tube.
Acquire and record 10,000 to 50,000 events in the tubes.
Check the Hoechst profile of viable (PI negative) cells using the Hoechst 33342 + PI-stained tube with optimized PMT settings.
Record a minimum of 500,000 events before establishing gates for primary spermatocytes.
Define and gate cells based on their Hoechst fluorescence pattern, which corresponds to their DNA content.
Gate 4N primary spermatocytes, based on their distinct sub-stages, following the contours of the cell density.
Program to collect and sort cells using a low flow rate with a 70 μm nozzle at 70 psi.
Maintain an event rate around 2,000–3,500 events/s.
Monitor the discard rate throughout to ensure it is preferably not >200 events/s.
Collect sorted cells in round bottom FACS tubes pre-loaded with collection media.
Pre-coat the interior of collection tubes with collection media to reduce the chances of sorted cells sticking during collection.
Enhance the survival of sorted fractions by using 10% FBS in collection media.
Centrifuge collected cells at 200 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in Freezing Media to a concentration of 1000 cells/μL.
Aliquot 100–200 μL of cell suspension into cryovials.
Store cryovials at −80°C.
Create an FSC-A versus SSC-A contour plot on BD FACS Diva software (linear scale).
Draw a “Scatter” gate to include cells of interest while excluding debris.
On the FSC-A versus FSC-H contour plot, create a sub-gate under the “Scatter” gate to encompass single cells.
Gate on PI negative live cells under the Singlets Gate using a PI-A versus FSC-A contour (log scale for PI-A, linear scale for FSC-A).
Create 2 gates and label them SSEA4- and SSEA4+ representing cells that are negatively or positively stained with anti-SSEA-4 APC-conjugated antibody.
Draw scatter gate from unstained control to include cells of interest while excluding debris.
Determine baseline voltages for the sample and level of autofluorescence in sample without adding fluorochromes.
Draw singlet gate to omit doublets which may contribute to false positives.
Gate on PI negative live cells from PI only control to determine cell viability.
Gate on SSEA-4 positive cells for collection.
Only use PI for control tubes.
Acquire and analyze the PI + SSEA-4 APC-conjugated Ab sample tube before establishing gates.
Record a minimum of 100,000 events.
Gates and select cells for SSEA-4 positivity.
Program to collect and sort PI negative SSEA-4-APC positive cells.
Sort cells using a low flow rate with a 70 μm nozzle at 70 psi.
Maintain an event rate around 2,000–3,500 events/s.
Monitor the discard rate throughout sorting.
Collect sorted cells in round bottom FACS tubes pre-loaded with collection media.
Pre-coat the interior of collection tubes with collection media to enhance survival.
Centrifuge collected cells at 200 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in Freezing Media to a concentration of 1000 cells/μL.
Mix 100-200 μL of cell suspension in cryovials.
Store the aliquots at -80°C.
